jobs.title: Design Human Factors Researcher, Apple Design Team
jobs.description:
Industrial Design (ID) at Apple focuses on the physical hardware experience, encompassing color, materials, finishes, digital sculpting, rendering, and physical prototyping. The discipline sits at the intersection of nearly every major function at the company, working seamlessly with Product Design Engineering, Manufacturing, Marketing, Human Interface Design, and Human Factors to bring ideas to life.  
  
The Apple Design Team is seeking a Human Factors Design Researcher. This is a fast-paced, collaborative position where you will need to understand how and who to work with to orchestrate a program plan and successfully manage execution of that plan. This individual will work with a variety of individuals both within and outside the Design team.  
  
**Description**  
  
An ideal candidate has a strong foundation in human factors research and understands how people interact with physical products. They can work across both high-level design concepts and detailed technical specifications. They are comfortable working directly with designers and engineers, communicate clearly, and ask the right questions to gather honest feedback. They balance technical rigor with strong intuition, translating research data into clear insights that improve the product experience.","responsibilities":"Plan and conduct user research studies (including physical prototype testing, anthropometric measurements, and usability evaluations) to inform early concepts and validate designs.  
  
Advocate for user needs, ergonomics, and accessibility across diverse populations throughout the design process.  
  
Collect and analyze both qualitative and quantitative data, including physical and behavioral measurements.  
  
Present research findings clearly and visually using experimental data and statistical analysis.  
  
Partner closely with Industrial Design, Product Design Engineering, Human Interface, and other cross-functional teams.  
  
Lead the design and execution of generative and evaluative research studies across hardware programs.  
  
Stay current on research methods, ergonomic standards, competitor products, and relevant literature.  
  
Prioritize and manage work across multiple concurrent projects.  
  
**Preferred Qualifications**  
  
Strong appreciation for physical design, aesthetics, and hardware details.  
  
Clear communication skills, with experience presenting technical findings to cross-functional partners and design leads.  
  
Experience working closely with industrial designers and engineers in a hands-on studio environment.  
  
Practical problem-solving skills when addressing complex or undefined design challenges.  
  
**Minimum Qualifications**  
  
Experience planning, conducting, and analyzing qualitative and quantitative human factors research.  
  
Ability to communicate complex research data and insights through clear visuals and concise summaries.  
  
Hands-on experience with physical human data collection methods (such as motion capture, anthropometry, pressure mapping, or biomechanical testing).  
  
Experience evaluating user interactions with physical hardware or wearable products.  
  
BS/BA in Human Factors, Ergonomics, HCI, Biomechanics, Cognitive Psychology, or a related field (Master’s or PhD preferred).  
  
In lieu of a degree, 10+ years of relevant industry experience.  
  
**Pay & Benefits**  
  
At Apple, base pay is one part of our total compensation package and is determined within a range. This provides the opportunity to progress as you grow and develop within a role. The base pay range for this role is between $184,700 and $324,800, and your base pay will depend on your skills, qualifications, experience, and location.  
  
Apple employees also have the opportunity to become an Apple shareholder through participation in Apple's discretionary employee stock programs. Apple employees are eligible for discretionary restricted stock unit awards, and can purchase Apple stock at a discount if voluntarily participating in Apple's Employee Stock Purchase Plan. You'll also receive benefits including: Comprehensive medical and dental coverage, retirement benefits, a range of discounted products and free services, and for formal education related to advancing your career at Apple, reimbursement for certain educational expenses - including tuition. Additionally, this role might be eligible for discretionary bonuses or commission payments as well as relocation. Learn more about Apple Benefits  
  
Note: Apple benefit, compensation and employee stock programs are subject to eligibility requirements and other terms of the applicable plan or program.

jobs.title: Senior Research Engineer, Robotics
jobs.description:
**About Tutor**

We believe robots are the biggest lever we have to making the physical world a better, more affordable place. But robots are a rounding error in our society: nearly nine out of ten American factories and warehouses don’t even have a single robot, and robots have yet to make their way into our homes or places of business.

Tutor Intelligence is changing that.

Tutor is a robotics research and deployment company, building generally capable robot hardware and artificial intelligence to enable robots to go where no robots have gone before. Sonny is a semi-humanoid robot with frontier dexterity approaching the human form. Cassie does back-breaking work, moving boxes, pallets, and bulk goods for businesses from family-owned manufacturers to some of the largest brands in the world. Tutor robots are manufactured at scale and operate as a network, combining the whole fleet’s learned experience to train ever more capable robot artificial intelligence.

Founded at MIT and headquartered in Watertown, MA, our team is full stack: we design and manufacture robot hardware, train our own models, work directly with the smallest and largest end-customers, and maintain our fleet across the United States. We’re a team of researchers, engineers, technicians, operators, and sellers who love building things and solving hard problems.

Our mission is grand: robots everywhere, for the common good, raising the standard of living across North America, and then the world.

**The Role**

Tutor's research team pushes the frontier of robot capability across the full stack. Researchers have access to 100+ robots for data collection and evaluation, a massive network of teleoperators, scaled hardware and manufacturing infrastructure, and the ability to collect real world data at enormous scale. Our work covers the complete lifecycle of real-world data generation and model training from initial behavior cloning to post-training with supervised fine-tuning and reinforcement learning. And researchers and research engineers work closely with applied engineers to develop novel techniques into robot products that can be deployed at scale.

As a research engineer on robotics, you'll turn research ideas into experiments that run on real robots, and make the results trustworthy.

### **What you'll work on**

* Build and run policy experiments on DF1, from task setup and data collection through rollouts and analysis.
* Own evaluation: task suites, success metrics, and tooling that make results comparable across robots, operators, and model versions.
* Build the robot-side software that runs policies: inference, control interfaces, safety limits, and logging.
* Improve the intervention loop, so teleoperators can step in when a policy fails and that data flows back into training.
* Debug failures that cross perception, control, hardware, and model behavior.
* Work with research scientists on what to try next, and with applied engineers on what's ready to deploy.

### **Requirements**

* Strong Python, and maintainable, tested code that runs on real hardware.
* Hands-on experience running learned policies or other autonomy on physical robots.
* Experience designing experiments and judging whether a result is real.
* Comfort debugging across Linux, networking, sensors, and robot control.

### **Nice to haves**

* Robot arms and manipulation; ROS or a similar framework.
* PyTorch and GPU inference.
* Teleoperation or VR systems.
* C++.

### **Why Tutor?**

Whether you’re designing robots, closing deals, running deployments, or creating the processes that help us scale, your work doesn’t sit on a shelf. It shows up on real production floors, making physical work safer and more affordable.

Our team of 160+ is driven by curiosity and a genuine love of building. Everyone here takes real ownership, learns fast, and holds a high bar while having each other’s backs. If you love hard problems and creating things that didn’t exist before, you’ll fit right in.

### **Benefits**

We take care of our team so they can do their best work. At Tutor, you’ll get:

* Fully employer-covered health insurance, so you’re protected without the premium.
* A managed 401(k) to help you plan for the future.
* Generous time off: unlimited PTO and all federal holidays off for full-time salaried employees, and 16+ days of accrued paid time off plus 1.5x pay on federal holidays for hourly employees.
* Regular in-office meals and team social events throughout the year.

As Tutor grows, so will our benefits. We’re continuing to invest in ways to support our team at work and beyond.

Tutor Intelligence is an equal opportunity employer and welcomes applicants from all backgrounds.
